questions.stem: Statement: In December 2024, the Indian government announced measures to achieve a GDP growth target of 6.5% to 7% for the current fiscal year. This decision followed slower-than-expected growth in the July-September quarter, attributed to weaker manufacturing and consumption sectors. The government plans to boost infrastructure spending and increase incentives for electric vehicle manufacturers to stimulate economic growth. Conclusions: I. The Indian government is proactively addressing the economic slowdown by implementing strategic measures. II. Enhancing infrastructure spending is expected to positively impact India's GDP growth. III. The slowdown in the July-September quarter was solely due to external global factors. Which of the above conclusions logically follows with the statement?
questions.explanation: Statement-conclusion logic. Conclusion I follows: the government announcing measures IS proactively addressing the slowdown. Conclusion II follows: the statement explicitly says infrastructure spending is being boosted to stimulate growth. Conclusion III does NOT follow: the statement attributes the slowdown to 'weaker manufacturing and consumption sectors' (domestic factors), not solely to external global factors. Therefore only I and II logically follow.

questions.stem: Statement: In October 2024, India and China reached an agreement to de-escalate border tensions, allowing both nations to resume patrolling in previously disputed areas along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). Despite the agreement, there remains a lack of trust between the two countries, and sporadic confrontations continue to occur in border regions. Proposed Courses of Action: 7 I. India should increase diplomatic engagements with China to build mutual trust and ensure the effective implementation of the agreement. II. India should enhance its military presence along the LAC to deter any potential aggression from China. III. India should seek mediation from international organizations to monitor and enforce the border agreement. Which of the above courses of action should India pursue to effectively address the ongoing challenges along the LAC?
questions.explanation: Course-of-action logic. Action I (increase diplomatic engagement to build trust) directly addresses the stated 'lack of trust' problem and is a standard diplomatic response — should be pursued. Action II (enhance military presence to deter aggression) is a prudent precaution given the agreement has not fully restored trust and sporadic confrontations continue — should be pursued. Action III (seek international mediation) is inconsistent with India's long-standing bilateralism doctrine and would not help resolve the specific operational issue of patrol coordination; should not be pursued. Hence Both I and II.
